pr_title: speed.c: Do not fail in -testmode if ASYNC_is_capable() returns false
pr_body:
ASYNC_is_capable() returns false on NonStop.
Fixes #25203

##### Checklist
<!-- Remove items that do not apply. For completed items, change [ ] to [x]. -->
- [x] tests are added or updated
pr_comments: The test worked now, but I do not understand it. We are in a thread model and async is enabled. Why would this fail as above?

I would prefer that this test checked `ASYNC_is_capable()` instead of being specific to NonStop. `getcontext()` may be supported at some point - in fact, I am surprised it is not. It may only be in the thread model I am using for this build. We have multiple models and PUT seems to be fine.

Sorry, didn't mean to suggest that we shouldn't check ASYNC_is_capable, we definately should, for cases where a platform may have a non-functional getcontext call only in some configurations.  I'm only suggesting that nonstop (I  think) likely doesn't support getcontext in any PUT thread model (at least thats my understanding from the technical library, I might be wrong.  SPT seems to have some support for it, but I believe you removed support for that model a while back.

as PUT doesn't seem to support getcontext(), I was suggesting that, instead of skipping the test, we modify the nonstop configs to build with no-async, so that the speed tests didn't try to do any async jobs at all, and you would save the code space incurred by adding those functions that would never do anything anyway.

I was actually testing with a new Kernel-level threading model that does not *yet* support `getcontext()`. PUT has been successfully passing this test for years (maybe not years, but no failures so far) and still does. NTL is not always up to date with PUT documentation, but don't tell anyone that I said that.
Sorry, @nhorman, I am actively testing on three different machines (two x86, one ia64 + different OS levels) at the moment and two different threading models.
ok, no worries, if PUT is working properly, but KLT is not, then it seems (i think) the right thing to do here is just disable async for KLT

> ok, no worries, if PUT is working properly, but KLT is not, then it seems (i think) the right thing to do here is just disable async for KLT

It is only that subtest that fails. The rest are fine.

I expect it's the only tests that use async jobs and expect them to function if compiled it.  Ssl record processing is the only other thing that I know if which uses async, and does so opportunistically

I've hit the same issue on OpenBSD. OpenBSD also lacks `getcontext()` function provided by libc. So running speed test fails with error detected at runtime.
```
lifty$ ./util/wrap.pl apps/openssl speed -async_jobs 1
speed: async_jobs specified but async not supported
speed: Use -help for summary.
```
IMO better way to fix it is to disable async mode on systems which lack `getcontext()` function.

I do have draft PR which fixes my OpenBSD itch. I feel we should extend this change for other OSes/platforms
where non-POSIX `getcontext()` function is not available.
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/25210

> PUT has been successfully passing this test for years (

The test is very new - only recently added to the repo.

Changed to a better way - just returning success from speed with -testmode if ASYNC_is_capable() returns false.

This will universally handle any non-capable platforms including OpenBSD @Sashan
Retesting... need a couple of hours.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been  updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.
Merged to the master branch. Thank you for the reviews.

issue_context.title: Weird failure in test_speed on NonStop
issue_context.body:
This just started...
```
speed: async_jobs specified but async not supported
speed: Use -help for summary.
../../util/wrap.pl ../../apps/openssl speed -testmode -async_jobs 1 => 1
not ok 14 - Test the async_jobs option
```
I'm not sure what to do with this situation.
comments: We just need to skip the testcase in the test_speed recipe.

review_comments: In my opinion, the `ASYNC_is_capable()` check should be performed first, followed by the `async_jobs` count check. Typically, we verify the supportability of a feature before checking other parameters or details.
Nope, this would break the test recipe.

silent success here doesn't make sense to me.  Just because ASYNC_is_capable returns 0, doesn't mean speed is incapable of functioning, it just means its only capable of running a single job at a time.  i.e. run time failure in getcontext is a problem, but its not fatal, the test can still continue as a non-async execution.

It seems like instead quietly doing nothing in test mode, we should issue a warning about async not being supported and reduce the async_jobs value to 0.

We extensively test speed in non-async mode. The point about the test which uses "-async_jobs" is to test the async jobs specific code which it cannot do if there is no async support. So it seems perfectly reasonable to me finish here.

The testmode is just for testing the speed command as of the test recipe, it will not do anything particularly useful apart from that and other (non -async_jobs) recipes exist anyway. There is no point in continuing.
